meta.title: Competitor Radar
meta.niche: Family location sharing, driving safety, and family-safety mobile apps

analysis.summary: Bark and Qustodio are the only ones publishing. Bark pushes buyers toward its phone and watch; Qustodio builds parent trust with research and guides. Life360 and the other three were quiet.

points.text: Bark updated 27 older pages and added 5 new ones, mostly comparisons and landing pages. It is refreshing pages that push buyers to its phone and watch.
Qustodio's 18 learning pages lean on research reports and parent guides, with 9 research pages updated. It is aiming at trust, not sales.
Life360 had 0 new and 0 updated pages in 30 days while Bark and Qustodio kept publishing. Life360 is silent on teen-safety topics they cover.

Life360.play: No new or updated pages in 30 days across 98 pages. No visible play this period.

Bark.play: Refreshes comparison pages against phone carriers and kids' watches. Adds a few guides on TikTok, gaming and iOS 27.

Qustodio.play: Publishes and refreshes original research, plus parent guides on AI apps, social media and phone readiness.

GeoZilla.play: No new or updated pages in 30 days. Small site of 15 pages.

Find My Kids.play: No new or updated pages in 30 days across 988 pages.

Google Family Link.play: No new or updated pages in 30 days. Most pages are international copies.

shared.title: Guides on new apps and platforms
shared.text: Bark covers TikTok and iOS 27. Qustodio covers Swerve AI and online impersonation. Both react to news parents worry about, so Life360 could join in.

shared.title: Teen wellbeing and social media talks
shared.text: Bark has teen mental health and gaming bullying pages. Qustodio has loneliness and peer-pressure pages. Both go beyond tracking into family conversations.

gaps.title: Location-sharing vs. kids' watches
gaps.text: Bark has 15 comparison pages, but they are about its own phone and watch. Nobody compares location-sharing apps head to head for parents.

gaps.title: Driving safety for teens
gaps.text: None of the active companies published driving-safety content this period. Life360 could own new-driver and teen-driving guides.

gaps.title: Original family-safety research
gaps.text: Only Qustodio publishes research (9 pages). Life360 could publish its own data on family location and driving habits.

versus.Bark: Bark ships comparison and landing pages aimed at buyers, and updated 27 pages. Life360 published and updated nothing in the same 30 days.
versus.Qustodio: Qustodio publishes research and parent guides and updated 15 pages. Life360 showed no new or updated content in the period.
versus.GeoZilla: GeoZilla is quiet like Life360, with no activity in 30 days and a much smaller site of 15 pages.
versus.Find My Kids: Find My Kids also had no activity in 30 days, though its site of 988 pages is far bigger than Life360's 98.
versus.Google Family Link: Google Family Link had no activity either. Its 129 pages are close to Life360's 98, and most are international copies.
